title: data labeling guidelines & samples - evelyn draft
content:
Purpose:
Quick working draft of cleanup rules, labeling edge cases, and sample mappings for the customer-support conversation dataset. This is a scratchpad - lots of TODOs and questions below. Use for annotator onboarding + as a reference when writing the final guidelines doc.

High-level goals:
- Make labels unambiguous and conservative where possible (prefer "unknown/needs-review" for ambiguous).
- Keep labels actionable for model training (clear tie to downstream behavior such as routing, escalation, and intent classification).
- Remove or normalize PII in text while preserving labelable intent.

Core label set (short):
- intent: {billing_issue, technical_issue, account_closure, feature_request, greeting, chitchat, refund_request, complaint, unknown}
- sentiment: {positive, neutral, negative, mixed}
- follow_up_required: {yes, no}
- sensitive: {pii_present, pii_removed}
- multi_intent: {single, multi}

Quick rules / heuristics:
1) PII handling:
   - Remove or redact explicit PII (emails, phone numbers, credit card numbers) in the content field but record sensitive=pii_present. Replace with placeholders: [EMAIL], [PHONE], [CC_NUM].
   - If PII contributes to label (e.g., mention of last 4 digits used to identify payment) annotate sensitive=pii_present and include a short rationale in the reviewer comment field (not in this doc).

2) Multi-intent detection:
   - If user asks two distinct requests in one message (e.g., "I want a refund and also close my account"), set multi_intent=multi and label primary intent as the one with highest downstream priority (refund_request > account_closure > technical_issue).
   - If both intents are equal priority, label primary as the first mentioned and add secondary in comments.

3) Ambiguous cases:
   - Vague phrasing: "I need help with my account" => intent=unknown, follow_up_required=yes. Annotator should flag for reviewer if >2 ambiguous in an annotator's batch.
   - Sarcasm: mark sentiment=negative if intent is clear; if not sure, sentiment=neutral and add needs_review tag.

4) System messages / agent text:
   - If the message is clearly from CSR/agent/system, label intent=system_message and exclude from training intent classification. Keep for dialog-state tracking only.

5) Short utterances:
   - Single token replies (e.g., "thanks", "ok") should be labeled as greeting/chitchat or positive depending on context. If impossible to determine, sentiment=neutral, intent=chitchat.

Samples (raw -> labeled):
1) Raw: "I was charged twice for April - want a refund asap."
   - intent: refund_request
   - sentiment: negative
   - follow_up_required: yes
   - sensitive: pii_removed
   - multi_intent: single
   - notes: customer explicitly requests refund; mark high priority.

2) Raw: "My app keeps crashing when I try to upload pics. Any fix?"
   - intent: technical_issue
   - sentiment: negative
   - follow_up_required: yes
   - sensitive: pii_removed
   - multi_intent: single

3) Raw: "Can you close my account? Also, stop charging me."
   - intent: multi (primary: refund_request, secondary: account_closure)
   - sentiment: negative
   - follow_up_required: yes
   - multi_intent: multi

4) Raw: "hello"
   - intent: greeting
   - sentiment: neutral
   - follow_up_required: no

5) Raw: "Is this included in the pro plan?" (no other context)
   - intent: unknown (needs follow up)
   - sentiment: neutral
   - follow_up_required: yes

Edge-case examples and decisions (notes):
- Bot/system prompts that include "if you need more help, click here" should not be treated as user intent but can be used to train escalation triggers.
- Payment provider error codes in user text: treat as technical_issue unless user explicitly requests refund. Map numeric codes to "provider_error" token during cleanup.
- Non-English tokens: if >30% of message is non-English, label language=<lang> in reviewer note and set intent=unknown. We will likely filter these out of the small-annotator pool.

Annotation workflow TODOs (operational notes):
- Add a "confidence" checkbox for annotators: high/medium/low. Low-confidence items go into a weekly review queue.
- Create a short 10-example golden set per label for initial QA (I can draft after we agree core label set).
- Decide whether to keep transcripts with timestamps or strip timestamps - timestamped messages can help dialog modeling but increase PII risk. Preference: strip exact timestamps, keep relative ordering.

Open questions / discussion points:
- Do we need a separate label for "billing question not related to charge" vs "refund_request"? My inclination: keep as billing_issue vs refund_request for clarity.
- How to handle repeated short tokens (e.g., "lol lol lol") - currently treat as chitchat unless the rest of message indicates sarcasm or intent.
- Should we add a label for "policy_violation" (profanity, hate speech)? Probably yes for moderation pipelines; add later.

Next steps (short):
- Iterate on this doc with Asha & Ryan; produce a 2-page final guidelines doc with 30 golden examples and 5 edge-case decision rules.
- Prepare annotator onboarding checklist (account setup, examples, quick QA).
- Implement placeholder-based cleanup script for PII and provider codes (Ryan to draft).

Notes to self: keep the guideline doc concise. Annotators lose interest after ~1 page of rules - use examples liberally and keep rules as short heuristics.

(end of scratchpad)
